findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0/untrusted-user restriction applied to website
findings.body: website is listed in untrusted_attributes (lines 105-111), whose generated include_website? hides it from anonymous viewers when scope.restrict_user_fields?(object) is true (e.g. a TL0 profile). The new website_name attribute is added to the plain attributes list but not to untrusted_attributes, so an anonymous viewer who may not see website still receives website_name, which contains the website host and, in the same-domain cases, the full path. This defeats the anti-spam/privacy restriction that hiding website is meant to enforce. website_name should be gated by the same restrict_user_fields? check ( taking care that a manually defined include_website_name? later in the class does not override the untrusted check).

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the '?' so the inclusion guard is never called
findings.body: The serializer framework and the rest of this file use the include_<attribute>? convention (e.g. include_email?, include_card_image_badge_id?, and the methods generated by staff_attributes/private_attributes/untrusted_attributes). The new method is named include_website_name without the question mark, so it will not be invoked when deciding whether to serialize website_name. As a result website_name is emitted even when website is blank (as a nil value) instead of being omitted, contrary to the guard's intent.

findings.title: Same-registrable-domain check misses the common www-host vs apex-host case
findings.body: The equal-length branch only handles sibling subdomains such as www.example.com vs forum.example.com. When the lengths differ it only checks whether the Discourse host ends with '.' + website_host. So website http://www.example.com/user on an instance at example.com falls into the else branch, example.com does not end with .www.example.com, and only 'www.example.com' is shown instead of the full path, while the reverse pairing (website example.com, instance www.example.com) does show the full path. The www/apex pairing is the most common same-domain configuration, so the feature silently does not work for it; the comparison should be based on the registrable domain rather than host-length and suffix checks.

findings.title: New website_name branches have no coverage for sibling subdomains or restricted viewers
findings.body: The added examples cover only unrelated hosts, an exact host match, and a parent-domain website, but not the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch in website_name (e.g. website www.example.com vs instance forum.example.com), the www-vs-apex pairing, or serialization of website_name for a TL0 user viewed anonymously. Those are precisely the branches with the non-trivial domain logic and the restriction interaction, so regressions or the bypass of the website restriction would not be caught by this spec.
